financials_interim.notes: Source: CHOT Interim Financial Statements for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (filed 14 Aug 2026, cdn.cse.lk/cmt/upload_report_file/545_1786703619990.06.2026.pdf). This PDF's embedded font has no usable ToUnicode/CID map -- pdftotext, pdfplumber and PyMuPDF text extraction all returned only replacement-character glyphs. Figures were transcribed by rendering each page to a 200dpi PNG and reading the tables visually (Statement of Comprehensive Income p.4, Statement of Financial Position p.3, Statement of Cash Flows p.7, notes pp.6-9). Group and Company columns are both disclosed -> two rows (GROUP, COMPANY) per project convention. COMPANY row. Ceylon Hotels Corporation PLC (the parent entity) is a pure holding company at Company level -- Revenue, Cost of Sales and Gross Profit are all nil ('-' in the filing) because all operating hotel revenue sits in subsidiaries (United Hotels Company Ltd, Tissa Resort, CHC Foods, The Kandy Hotels Company (1938) PLC, Suisse Hotels, Air Line Services, Ceylon Hotels Maldives) consolidated only at Group level. Company-level profit (Rs.14,992k PAT) comes almost entirely from Finance Income of Rs.17,383k (interest on inter-company loans to subsidiaries/JVs, Note 9 p.7 -- e.g. Rs.9,562k from Ceylon Hotels Holdings (Pvt) Ltd, the parent, and Rs.4,515k from Ceylon Holiday Holdings (Pvt) Ltd, a JV) less Admin Expenses of Rs.1,808k; no Company-level Finance Cost is disclosed this quarter (nil, vs Rs.121k a year earlier). total_liabilities (current only, Rs.45,953k) = Trade and other payables Rs.2,407k + Amounts due to related companies Rs.43,546k; no non-current liabilities disclosed at Company level. capex, cash_from_investing and cash_from_financing are all nil at Company level per the cash flow statement (p.7) -- the Company itself made no PPE purchases or financing movements this quarter. Balance sheet identity check: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity (2,851,175 = 45,953 + 2,805,222, exact). PBT - Tax = PAT check: 15,575 - 583 = 14,992, exact.

Operating_profit uses CHOT's own explicit 'Profit/(loss) from operations' line (p.4): Rs.(48,972)k, i.e. Revenue - Cost of Sales + Other Operating Income - Selling & Distribution Exp - Admin Exp - Other Operating Exp. short_term_borrowings combines the current 'Interest-bearing borrowings' (Rs.172,515k) and 'Bank overdrafts' (Rs.277,635k) lines from the BS (p.3), both current-liability debt instruments; long_term_borrowings is the non-current 'Interest-bearing borrowings' line (Rs.844,740k). trade_payables is 'Trade and other payables' (Rs.478,091k, current) -- CHOT does not separately split trade vs other payables. capex (Rs.16,223k) = 'Acquisition of property, plant & equipment' per the cash flow statement (p.7). Group PBT/PAT are losses this quarter; the widening of the loss from PBT (Rs.(54,205)k) to PAT (Rs.(70,652)k) is because Income tax was a net EXPENSE of Rs.16,447k this period (vs a net tax REVERSAL/credit of Rs.31,217k in Q1 FY2025/26) -- a swing that itself pushed the loss wider even before considering the operating and JV-share drivers discussed in interim_updates. No segment note is disclosed (Note 3, p.6, states 'there are no distinguishable components to be identified as segments for the company') and no occupancy-rate or average-room-rate data is disclosed anywhere in this filing -- see gaps_note in interim_updates. interim_updates.note_text: Ceylon Hotels Corporation PLC (CHOT) reported Group revenue of Rs.438.0mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 25.1% YoY from Rs.350.1mn, and the Group operating loss narrowed 36.6% YoY to Rs.(49.0)mn (from Rs.(77.2)mn), with Selling & Distribution Expenses up 117.2% YoY to Rs.(50.6)mn (from Rs.(23.3)mn) -- a sharp step-up in marketing/distribution spend that partly offset the operating improvement from higher revenue and gross profit (+33.8% YoY to Rs.318.2mn from Rs.237.8mn). Despite the narrower operating loss, the Group's bottom line went the other way: the net loss attributable to equity holders WIDENED to Rs.(61.7)mn from Rs.(33.8)mn a year earlier (total Group loss Rs.(70.7)mn vs Rs.(50.6)mn, +39.6%), driven by two below-the-operating-line items: the Group's Share of loss of equity-accounted investees (the JVs Ceylon Holidays Holding (Pvt) Ltd, CHC Rest House (Pvt) Ltd and Suisse Hotel Kandy (Pvt) Ltd) jumped to Rs.(53.3)mn from just Rs.(5.4)mn a year earlier -- an increase of Rs.47.8mn (+881%) that is by itself larger than the entire net-loss deterioration -- and a net foreign exchange GAIN that, while itself up 338.9% YoY to Rs.41.0mn (from Rs.9.3mn), was not large enough to offset the JV swing. Net finance income improved sharply, up from just Rs.0.8mn to Rs.48.0mn, on both higher finance income (+40.8% YoY to Rs.70.3mn) and the FX gain. Company-level (parent-only) profit rose 31.5% YoY to Rs.15.0mn (from Rs.11.4mn), almost entirely on finance income of Rs.17.4mn (+49.2% YoY) earned on inter-company loans to subsidiaries and JVs (Note 9, p.7) -- the Company itself has no operating revenue, being a pure holding entity for United Hotels Company Ltd, Tissa Resort, CHC Foods, The Kandy Hotels Company (1938) PLC, Suisse Hotels, Air Line Services and Ceylon Hotels Maldives. No occupancy-rate, average-room-rate or tourism-season commentary is disclosed anywhere in this filing (see gaps_note).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for CHOT in this database, so no prior quarter (Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) no occupancy rate, average room rate (ARR), or RevPAR data is disclosed anywhere in this filing, despite the explicit instruction to check for it -- CHOT's interim filings are bare financial statements with no MD&A/operational commentary section; (2) Note 3 (p.6) explicitly states there are no distinguishable business segments, so no per-hotel or per-subsidiary revenue/profit breakdown is available to explain which properties drove the 25.1% Group revenue growth; (3) the Rs.47.8mn swing in Share of loss of equity-accounted investees (JVs) is not explained by name or cause beyond the JV entity names listed in Note 1 (p.6: Ceylon Holidays Holding (Pvt) Ltd, CHC Rest House (Pvt) Ltd, Suisse Hotel Kandy (Pvt) Ltd) -- no commentary is given on which JV(s) drove the loss or why; (4) no tourism-season, arrivals, or FX-exposure-on-foreign-currency-debt commentary is disclosed (the Group's interest-bearing borrowings, Rs.1,017,255k combined current+non-current, are not identified as LKR or foreign-currency in this filing). This PDF's font also could not be machine-extracted (see notes field) -- all figures were read from rendered page images rather than programmatic text/table extraction, so extra manual cross-checks (balance sheet identity, PBT-tax=PAT) were applied and passed for both GROUP and COMPANY rows.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group revenue grew 25.1% YoY to Rs.438.0mn and the operating loss narrowed 36.6% to Rs.(49.0)mn, but the Group's net loss WIDENED 39.6% YoY to Rs.(70.7)mn because the Share of loss of equity-accounted investees (the Group's hotel JVs) jumped 881% YoY to Rs.(53.3)mn from Rs.(5.4)mn -- a Rs.47.8mn swing larger than the entire net-loss deterioration. A 117.2% jump in selling & distribution costs also ate into the operating improvement. Company-level (parent-only) profit rose 31.5% to Rs.15.0mn purely on inter-company finance income, since the Company itself has no trading revenue -- all hotel operations sit in subsidiaries and JVs.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 25.1% YoY to Rs.438.0mn (from Rs.350.1mn); gross profit up 33.8% YoY to Rs.318.2mn (from Rs.237.8mn)
Group operating loss narrowed 36.6% YoY to Rs.(49.0)mn (from Rs.(77.2)mn) despite Selling & Distribution Expenses rising 117.2% YoY to Rs.(50.6)mn (from Rs.(23.3)mn)

Share of loss of equity-accounted investees (JVs: Ceylon Holidays Holding, CHC Rest House, Suisse Hotel Kandy) rose to Rs.(53.3)mn from Rs.(5.4)mn a year earlier -- an 881% increase (Rs.47.8mn swing) that is the single largest driver of the Group's net-loss widening
Net foreign exchange gain up 338.9% YoY to Rs.41.0mn (from Rs.9.3mn); net finance income up to Rs.48.0mn from Rs.0.8mn -- both improved but not enough to offset the JV-loss swing
Group net loss attributable to equity holders widened to Rs.(61.7)mn from Rs.(33.8)mn a year earlier (total Group loss Rs.(70.7)mn vs Rs.(50.6)mn, +39.6%); loss per share Rs.(0.34) vs Rs.(0.19)

Company-level (parent-only) profit up 31.5% YoY to Rs.15.0mn (from Rs.11.4mn), driven by finance income of Rs.17.4mn (+49.2% YoY) on inter-company loans -- the Company has no trading revenue, being a pure holding entity for its hotel subsidiaries and JVs

No segment note disclosed (Note 3, p.6: 'there are no distinguishable components to be identified as segments for the company'); no occupancy or average-room-rate data disclosed anywhere in the filing
key_drivers: Share of loss of equity-accounted investees rose to Rs.(53.3)mn from Rs.(5.4)mn (+881% YoY, a Rs.47.8mn swing) -- the single largest driver of the Group's net loss widening from Rs.(50.6)mn to Rs.(70.7)mn, and larger than the entire deterioration by itself
Selling & Distribution Expenses +117.2% YoY (Rs.23,269k to Rs.50,550k) partly offset the benefit of 25.1% revenue growth and 33.8% gross-profit growth at the operating-profit line

Net foreign exchange gain +338.9% YoY (Rs.9,333k to Rs.40,956k) and finance income +40.8% YoY (Rs.49,916k to Rs.70,272k) together lifted net finance income to Rs.48.0mn from Rs.0.8mn -- partially cushioning the JV-loss swing but not enough to prevent the net loss from widening
Income tax swung from a net Rs.31,217k reversal/credit (2025) to a Rs.16,447k net expense (2026), a Rs.47.7mn negative swing that further widened the loss from PBT to PAT
